artifact_provenance.input: Exact release artifact or locally built candidate bound to full repository commit and SHA-256 digest.
artifact_provenance.rejection: Floating refs, uncommitted source, a mismatched binary digest, or an unpinned MCP checkout fail during preparation.
artifact_provenance.record: Receipt records repository commits, binary digest, MCP executable digest, Factory commit, and profile digest.

service_contract.install: Use the shipped onboarding install path under a disposable operator HOME.
service_contract.manager: Use the native user service manager for the selected platform lane.
service_contract.health: Observe the production loopback status and capability endpoints after manager-reported startup.
service_contract.restart: Terminate or stop the manager-owned daemon and require the manager to start a fresh process.
service_contract.isolation: Use a unique operator home, loopback port, and service identity that cannot target an existing user installation.

product_route_contract.registry: Seed at least two reopenable Product event-store routes through production Product creation or migration paths.
product_route_contract.bindings: Create per-Product workspace bindings through the production MCP-to-ToolRequest path.
product_route_contract.routing: Every Product-scoped MCP operation selects a daemon-validated Product and emits ToolRequest.product_id.
product_route_contract.rehydration: After a fresh service process starts, registry routes and workspace bindings reopen from operator-local persistence.

fault_contract.scope: Fault injection may alter only one disposable Product workspace-binding record after its digest is recorded.
fault_contract.assertion: The damaged Product reports repair-required while another Product remains routable and readable.
fault_contract.recovery: Restore the recorded binding bytes before teardown; never synthesize a healthy response.

teardown_contract.service: Stop and uninstall the exact disposable service identity even after an assertion failure.
teardown_contract.processes: Terminate only child processes whose identities were recorded by the runner.
teardown_contract.files: Remove disposable operator roots after verifying the service manager no longer references them.
teardown_contract.failure: A teardown failure makes the run non-terminal and requires owner review before retry.

honest_limit: The profile remains partial until both the macOS launchd-user and Linux systemd-user lanes have terminal real-process evidence using a released artifact and a production MCP build that validates Product selection and sends product_id on every Product-scoped ToolRequest.
